title: Strictly No Elephants
read: Read 2 · Retelling, sequencing, and summarizing the story
teacherNotes: Retell events using illustrations (RL.PK.2, RL.PK.6), express ideas (SL.PK.6), show empathy (SEL 5), and recognize diversity and respect others (SEL 6). Listen for how children retell the story, what prompting they need, their understanding of friendship and diversity, and how they express thoughts. Prepare self-portraits or photographs of self-portraits from Unit 1, Weeks 7–8, and flag printed page 22.

steps.note: As we read I will ask you to remember and retell what happened in the book, and we’ll also talk about some of the illustrations.

steps.title: After Reading · Self-Portraits
steps.note: Show the illustration on printed page 22 and teacher-held self-portraits from Unit 1. “I mentioned before that this illustration reminds me of the self portraits we made in Unit 1.” Invite responses. No children’s photographs or self-portraits are stored in this reader.

steps.title: Different Skin Tones · All Friends
steps.prompt: They have darker skin tones, lighter skin tones, and they’re all friends.
steps.note: Your self portraits have different skin tones, because your skin colors are different. Just like in this illustration, we can see the boy and his friends have many different skin tones. If there is limited variation among children’s skin tones in the class, consider the photographs in the Week 4 Art Studio Learning Experience, Skin Tone Color Mixing.

steps.title: Closing
steps.prompt: We’ll read it again tomorrow and act out the story.
steps.note: Today we read Strictly No Elephants for the second time.
